derivations.quote: Claim: at each vertex $v$ the stored array equals $D_v g$, with $g$ the logical array there. The claim holds at the sources by the definition of $g$. It passes along an edge by applying $D_vD_u^{-1}$. It passes through a pointwise linear gate $G$ with $z$ incoming arrays, since $G(D_v g_1,\dots,D_v g_z)=D_v\,G(g_1,\dots,g_z)$ by linearity. Induction carries it to the sinks, so the network maps $f$ to $D_{\rm out}\,\mathsf S_\Omega\,D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$.

Take a route from a source $q$ through a gate $x$ to a sink $p$. Its edge operators $D_xD_q^{-1}$ and $D_pD_x^{-1}$ multiply to $D_pD_q^{-1}$, so the frame $D_x$ cancels. For a signed role permutation sending input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w$, each route applies $\varepsilon_w D_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ to its array, auxiliary roles included. So interior frames can be chosen to make each edge cheap.

relations.quote: Frames act on the wires of the [Linear exchange network with restored scratch wires](linear-network.md) once each scalar is replaced by an array indexed by a finite address set $\Omega$ common to all wires.
Each frame is checked invertible by the rank criterion of [Rank, subspaces and orthogonal complements](linear-algebra-basics.md): it has full rank, so $D_v^{-1}$ exists.

symbols.name: vertex
symbols.meaning: A source, gate or sink of the network.
symbols.quote: Each source, gate and sink $v$ carries an invertible linear operator $D_v$ on arrays indexed by $\Omega$, called its frame.

symbols.name: frame
symbols.meaning: The invertible linear operator on arrays indexed by $\Omega$ assigned to vertex $v$.
symbols.quote: Each source, gate and sink $v$ carries an invertible linear operator $D_v$ on arrays indexed by $\Omega$, called its frame.

symbols.name: address set
symbols.meaning: The finite set of addresses indexing the array on every wire, common to all wires.
symbols.quote: Frames act on the wires of the [Linear exchange network with restored scratch wires](linear-network.md) once each scalar is replaced by an array indexed by a finite address set $\Omega$ common to all wires.

symbols.name: network on arrays
symbols.meaning: The network acting on the vector of wire arrays.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathsf S_\Omega$ denote the network acting on these arrays; its scalar gates act pointwise, address by address.

symbols.name: tail vertex
symbols.quote: An edge from a vertex $u$ to a vertex $v$ applies $D_vD_u^{-1}$ to the wire's array, so the logical array is stored in frame $D_u$ before the edge and $D_v$ after it.

symbols.name: role
symbols.meaning: A wire's fixed place in the network, indexing input and output roles.
symbols.quote: A wire's fixed place in the network is its role $w$.

symbols.name: source of a role
symbols.meaning: The source at which input role $w$ starts.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathrm{source}(w)$ be the source of input role $w$.

symbols.name: sink of a role
symbols.meaning: The sink at which output role $w$ ends.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathrm{sink}(w)$ be the sink of output role $w$.

symbols.name: input frame
symbols.meaning: The block-diagonal sum of the source frames over all roles.
symbols.quote: Let $D_{\rm in}=\bigoplus_w D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}$ and $D_{\rm out}=\bigoplus_w D_{\mathrm{sink}(w)}$ be their block-diagonal sums over all roles.

symbols.name: output frame
symbols.meaning: The block-diagonal sum of the sink frames over all roles.
symbols.quote: Let $D_{\rm in}=\bigoplus_w D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}$ and $D_{\rm out}=\bigoplus_w D_{\mathrm{sink}(w)}$ be their block-diagonal sums over all roles.

symbols.name: supplied input
symbols.meaning: The physical input array supplied to the network.
symbols.quote: A supplied input $f$ has logical array $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$.

symbols.name: logical array
symbols.meaning: The array the network computes with at a vertex, so that the stored array is its frame applied to it.
symbols.quote: A supplied input $f$ has logical array $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$.

symbols.name: pointwise linear gate
symbols.meaning: A scalar gate applied at each address, linear in its inputs.
symbols.quote: It passes through a pointwise linear gate $G$ with $z$ incoming arrays, since $G(D_v g_1,\dots,D_v g_z)=D_v\,G(g_1,\dots,g_z)$ by linearity.

symbols.name: gate fan-in
symbols.meaning: The number of wire arrays entering a gate.
symbols.quote: It passes through a pointwise linear gate $G$ with $z$ incoming arrays, since $G(D_v g_1,\dots,D_v g_z)=D_v\,G(g_1,\dots,g_z)$ by linearity.

symbols.name: source on a route
symbols.meaning: The source at which the route starts.
symbols.quote: Take a route from a source $q$ through a gate $x$ to a sink $p$.

symbols.name: gate on a route
symbols.meaning: The gate through which the route passes.
symbols.quote: Take a route from a source $q$ through a gate $x$ to a sink $p$.

symbols.name: sink on a route
symbols.meaning: The sink at which the route ends.
symbols.quote: Take a route from a source $q$ through a gate $x$ to a sink $p$.

symbols.name: role permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation sending each input role to an output role.
symbols.quote: For a signed role permutation sending input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w$, each route applies $\varepsilon_w D_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ to its array, auxiliary roles included.

symbols.name: sign of a role
symbols.meaning: The scalar sign with which the route of input role $w$ is multiplied.
symbols.quote: For a signed role permutation sending input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w$, each route applies $\varepsilon_w D_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ to its array, auxiliary roles included.
